title: I always believed 90% of traders lose because they are just bad at trading. Then I actually read the SEBI study and realised I had the whole story wrong.
author: Electronic_Tea_2948
selftext:
Everyone throws around that "90% of F&O traders lose money" line. I used to nod along and quietly assume it meant most people are undisciplined, and that I would obviously be in the smart 10% if I just tried harder.

Then I went and read what SEBI's study actually found, and it changed how I see the whole thing.

Yes, nine out of ten individual traders lost money in F&O over the three-year period studied. But the part nobody repeats is the scale. Aggregate losses by individual traders crossed ₹1.81 lakh crore, and the average loss per trader was around ₹50,000. That is not pocket change for a normal household. This was not a handful of gamblers, it was a structural bleed hitting lakhs of ordinary people.

Here is the reframe that got me. SEBI did not conclude that traders were the problem. It concluded the structure was. The specific combination of daily expiries, tiny sub ten lakh contract sizes, premium that was not collected upfront, and almost no real time monitoring had created conditions where undercapitalised retail speculation was being facilitated at scale. The setup itself was tilted toward blowups, and the regulator went and changed the setup. Jainam

I found that both freeing and humbling. Freeing because a lot of past losses were the structure doing exactly what it was built to do, not proof that I am hopeless. Humbling because "just try harder" was never going to fix a structural problem. I need a real edge and real risk control, not more screen time.

Has reading the actual numbers changed how anyone else thinks about their own losses? Feels like a lot of us spent years blaming only ourselves when the table was tilted from the start.
